sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with commercial law statutes and limited common-law influence)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT), as amended; Law 52 of 24 October 2016 (Due Diligence for Legal Persons); Executive Decrees No. 128 of 2017 and No. 254 of 2017 (UBO Registry); Law 70 of 2014 on Private Interest Foundations; Regulation of the Panama Public Registry on Private Interest Foundations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (where Apostille Convention not applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Extract of Beneficial Owner's Home-Country Company Registry (if UBO is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization with Spanish sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport / Government-issued Identification of all UBOs, Directors, and Protectors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority in the respective person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy and Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Bank Reference Letter and Professional Standing Certificate for UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO's financial institution or professional body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter; notarized attestation of signature (legalization not mandatory but recommended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against national and international sanction lists, including UN, OFAC, EU, and UK consolidated lists. Enhanced due diligence is applied to PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and large-value transactions; all due diligence findings must be documented, retained, and filed with the resident agent under Law 23 and Law 52.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) Electronic Name Clearance System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All foundation names must be in Spanish or an accepted Latin-script transliteration. The name must include a distinguishing designation and may include the suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'PIF.' Names causing confusion with existing registrations or containing unapproved foreign script are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration motion through a Panamanian attorney within 15 business days. The Registrar must respond within 30 business days. If still rejected, an administrative appeal may be filed with the higher administrative body of the Public Registry, followed by judicial review before the Administrative Litigation Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted as the statutory registered office. A physical office of a licensed resident agent in Panama is mandatory. While administrative and back-office operations may be virtualized for this no-code software business, the registered agent must maintain physical presence and fully accept service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk of unannounced inspection for a clean, low-risk no-code software activity. However, the Financial Intelligence Unit and the Public Registry may conduct risk-based inspections under Law 23 if red flags arise; estimated probability below 5% per annum for compliant structures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Panama Public Registry incorporation fee (PIF charter filing and registration)
Name clearance and corporate name reservation certificate
Notarization of foundation charter by Panamanian notary
Resident agent and registered office service — first year
Apostille/consular legalization of origin documents (bundle of UBO and supporting papers)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign Competent Apostille Authority / Panamanian Consulate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Registry filing and AML/CFT due diligence processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Financial Intelligence Unit (through Public Registry)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of foreign-language documents (if any)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995), as amended by Law 41 of 2000 and Law 5 of 2013; core sections: Arts. 4-12 (creation, endowment and registration), Art. 19 (Foundation Council), Art. 25 (by-laws) and Art. 40 (resident agent requirement)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Section of Private Interest Foundations
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado), protocolized before a Notary Public and recorded in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared in the Charter; actual contribution may be deferred and no bank escrow deposit is required by law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the Foundation Council of [Foundation Name], held in Panama City on [Date], the following resolutions were adopted unanimously: FIRST, acceptance of the Foundation Charter and of the initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared therein. SECOND, designation of the registered office at the offices of [Resident Agent], Panama City, Republic of Panama. THIRD, appointment of [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Treasurer of the Foundation Council. FOURTH, authorization of the President and Secretary jointly to open banking and payments accounts with Stripe and Paddle, to execute platform agreements, and to instruct counsel to complete registration with the Public Registry and tax authorities. FIFTH, adoption of the internal by-laws (Reglamento). APPROVED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Panamanian Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Law firm led by a licensed Panamanian attorney (abogado idóneo) in good standing with the Corte Suprema de Justicia, acting as resident agent (agente residente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter appointing the resident agent, who will verify the identity of founders and beneficiaries, conduct due diligence, and prepare the Charter and by-laws. The resident agent must be maintained continuously under Law 25 of 1995.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport of each founder
Utility bill or bank reference evidencing residential address
Corporate profile of any corporate founder (certificate of good standing)
Declaration of ultimate beneficial owners (initial draft)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: None expected at this stage; if the attorney identifies AML/KYC deficiencies, obtain corrected or notarially apostilled documents and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Notary Public) of Panama City, Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Charter (Acta Constitutiva) and by-laws (Reglamento) in Spanish or bilingual form, specifying the foundation name, initial endowment, beneficiaries, council members, registered office, purpose (provision of visual web template and low-code web application builder services) and asset disposition rules. Execute the Charter before the Notary and obtain the protocolized first-transcript copy.
required_dossiers: Draft of the Foundation Charter
Draft of the by-laws (Reglamento)
Passport copies of all council members
Proof of acceptance by each council member
Payment of notarial fees (approximate USD 150-250)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary raises formal objections, amend the drafting errors and re-execute; any clerical defect can be corrected by a notarial correction page (nota de corrección).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Official State Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) and Dirección de Ingresos del Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official state registration fee of USD 300 via the official bank deposit slip (planilla) corresponding to the Public Registry, and attach the receipt to the filing packet. Additional small fees may apply for certified copies.
required_dossiers: Official fee payment form of the Registro Público de Panamá
Bank deposit receipt for USD 300
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied, request a bank certification and rectification from the Registro Público treasury office before submitting the Charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Section of Private Interest Foundations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Charter, the by-laws (if not incorporated by reference) and the fee receipt with the Public Registry for inscription. The Registry examines the Charter for legality and compliance with Law 25 of 1995 and issues the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Protocolized copy of the Foundation Charter
Copy of the by-laws (Reglamento)
Original bank receipt for state fees
Resident agent acceptance letter and address
Legal size paper copies in the Registry's prescribed format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (nota de defecto), file a corrective addendum (adenda) or clarification within ten (10) business days; if the defect is irremediable, re-protocolize a conforming Charter and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Collection of Registration Certificate and Certified Copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon inscription, collect the Certificado de Registro and request certified copies (copias cotejadas o autenticadas) of the Charter. These documents constitute conclusive evidence of the foundation's legal existence and are required for bank, tax and payment-platform onboarding.
required_dossiers: Expediente number assigned by the Registry
Payment of certified-copy issuance fees (approximate USD 25-50)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certified copies contain typographical errors, request immediate correction (corrección de oficio) from the Registry within five (5) business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Beneficial Ownership Filing and Optional Municipal Operations Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía de Panamá (Municipality of Panama); Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the RUC tax identification number for banking and payment platform purposes and file the beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) with the DGI per Law 129 of 2020. If the foundation maintains physical offices or conducts local activities, obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación from the Alcaldía; for wholly offshore digital operations, the municipal license is not mandatory. Commence the statutory books (minutes book and registry of members/council).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Passport copies of council members and resident agent acceptance
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
Completion of DGI RUC registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries the beneficial ownership filing, submit the definitive shareholder/foundation-beneficiary schedule and supporting KYC documents; the RUC can be issued provisionally pending review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - not applicable: software publishing and no-code web application building are treated as non-industrial digital services and do not require an industrial manufacturing permit under Panamanian law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required for digital no-code website builder services; optional municipal Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business License) applies only if a physical office or local commercial presence is established in Panama

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registration / Diagnóstico Ambiental) - low-impact administrative office and digital services activity; full EIA report (Categoría III) not required; an environmental registration is only triggered if a physical office exceeding thresholds or significant waste generation is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds under MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0423-2009 and General Environmental Law (Ley 41 de 1998): domestic office wastewater and graywater must meet pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 below 200 mg/L and TSS below 200 mg/L prior to discharge to municipal sewer; no VOC or industrial air emission sources are generated by pure software activity; electronic waste (computers, servers, peripherals) must be delivered to authorized e-waste recyclers, with waste manifests retained for inspection

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If physical offices are established, obtain: (i) fire safety inspection and certificate (Visto Bueno) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; (ii) structural and land-use clearance from the Municipality (Alcaldía) under the national building and zoning regulations; and (iii) occupational health clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) for office workplaces, including emergency exits, electrical safety and ergonomic standards. For fully remote or outsourced operations, no physical clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); principal online portal: Sistema de Gestión de Ingresos (SIGIR) / e-Tax at https://etax.mef.gob.pa and https://www.dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is registered in the Registro Público de Panamá; for tax purposes it must request a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI portal or at the DGI offices only if the entity is engaged in activities generating Panamanian-source income or is required by a Panamanian counterparty or bank to present a tax ID. The PIF's resident agent (Apoderado) completes the contributor registration form, presents the foundation certificate and the generic status from the Public Registry, appoints a fiscal representative if applicable, and obtains the RUC and ITBMS registration in the same procedure. For a pure offshore PIF with no Panama-source commercial activity and no digital services sales into Panama, no RUC or ITBMS registration is statutorily required, but financial institutions may request a RUC or an affidavit of non-tax liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a territorial source-of-income system without US-style check-the-box elections. A PIF is not classified for tax as a pass-through trust; it is a separate legal person taxed at entity level only on Panama-source income. The foundation may elect to carry on no taxable activity as a pure asset-holding vehicle or may elect to submit an annual tax return when it receives Panama-source income. Special regime elections include Multinational Headquarters (SEM) under Law 41/2007 and Free Zone/City of Knowledge incentives; no hybrid mismatch or transparent entity elections exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold for ITBMS registration; any person habitually transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register. However, small taxpayers with annual gross income up to B/.250,000 may use the simplified small-taxpayer regime (régimen de pequeños contribuyentes), which replaces the ordinary ITBMS return with a simplified monthly quota.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has phased mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) via the DGI Facturación en Línea/SFE platform. Invoices must be issued in DGI-validated XML/JSON formats with a unique digital stamp (clave de aceptación), a QR code, and sequential fiscal authorization. Medium and large taxpayers must transmit invoices in near real-time using DGI-approved API/REST endpoints or the certified web portal; the DGI performs before-issuance authentication and returns acceptance or rejection codes. Credit notes, debit notes, and payment receipts follow the same electronic flow; exports must be marked with the zero-rated indicator.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported out of Panamanian customs territory are zero-rated under ITBMS if the exporter is registered and the sale is evidenced by a valid export customs declaration and transport document. Services are treated as exported and zero-rated when the recipient is located abroad, the service is not physically or legally connected to Panama, and the benefit is received and used outside Panama; supporting contracts and payment evidence must identify the non-resident beneficiary. Merely invoicing a foreign customer from Panama is insufficient; the exporter must demonstrate that the economic effect of the operation occurs abroad. Input ITBMS related to zero-rated exports may be refunded through the saldo a favor mechanism after DGI verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas de Exportación / DEX) endorsed by Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas
Transport document — original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panama
Final Commercial Invoice and Packing List identifying foreign buyer and export terms
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice for payment of exported goods/services
Copy of export contract or service agreement and non-resident beneficiary's tax identity evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims up to six years from the filing deadline, and this period becomes unlimited in cases of non-filing or fraudulent intent. If documents are false, missing, or the goods or services are not in fact exported, the DGI claws back all zero-rated output VAT, disallows associated input VAT credits, and imposes a surcharge of 1.5% per month plus statutory interest. Tax evasion penalties range from 100% to 200% of the tax omitted; use of falsified export declarations can trigger criminal prosecution under Ley 38/2004 and customs smuggling sanctions. The absence of a Panamanian exchange-control regime means the 180-day remittance term is a documentary benchmark rather than a strict currency requirement, but failure to show collection can still defeat the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá; Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) regulates licensed banks; the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) oversees fiscal matters. Panama does not operate a traditional central bank issuing national fiat currency; the U.S. dollar is the legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with no central exchange control regime. Capital and current account transactions are generally free from convertibility restrictions. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriations by Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are permissible without prior central bank approval, provided the foundation is in good standing, economic substance obligations (where applicable) are satisfied, and the remittance is effected through a licensed Panama banking entity or recognized international clearing channel. No surrender requirements or FX licensing hurdles exist for inbound or outbound flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts may be held freely in U.S. dollars or any other convertible currency, and may be disbursed offshore without repatriation obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately viable with legal constraints. Panama recognizes digital wallet operators and payment service providers under SBP regulation, but non-licensed offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) cannot directly open settlement accounts in Panama regulated banks without a local license or a formal correspondent banking arrangement. An offshore EMI may be used only as a payment collection conduit, not as the primary treasury clearing rail, unless it is licensed by the SBP or operates under a recognized fintech passport arrangement. Adverse regulatory perception and de-risking policies of correspondent banks increase the compliance burden; therefore, the PIF should maintain a primary bank relationship with a Tier 1 Panama licensed bank and use EMIs strictly for merchant acquiring and low-value SaaS subscription collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the foundation council members and the resident agent is generally required for the initial KYC due diligence of a PIF. Most Tier 1 Panama banks mandate in-person identity verification for the founder, the foundation council, and the resident agent before opening an account, either at the bank's Panama branch or at a notarized Panama consulate abroad under limited remote protocols. Fully remote account opening is uncommon and typically restricted to low-risk, pre-approved corporate structures with strong existing banking references. The foundation's registered agent in Panama must be physically present for all bank meetings; beneficial owners must provide certified passport copies, original or notarized apostilled documents, professional references, and source-of-funds declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF structure viewed as opaque nominee vehicle, especially where the founder is not the ultimate beneficial owner or where the foundation council is a licensed professional firm with no commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart of the PIF; certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Regulations; notarized register of council members and beneficiaries; sworn declaration of economic substance and purpose; audited financial statements or internal management accounts; valid passports and proof of residence of all council members and beneficial owners; professional references from the founding lawyer and the resident agent; source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, share sale contracts, or inheritance documents); tax residence certificates of all material parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue from low-code SaaS operations routed through multiple payment intermediaries without a clear end-client invoice trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS subscription agreements and end-user licenses; invoicing schedule matching Stripe/Paddle payout reports; subsidiary platform transaction logs; beneficiary/ultimate-controller identification for all payment processors; detailed breakdown of recurring revenues against delivered digital services; compliance policy for refunds and chargebacks; data processing agreements under applicable privacy law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of direct bank-interview attendance by a substantive executive or use of remote KYC only, raising risk of perceived shell or fronting structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Minutes of the foundation council resolution authorizing the account; power of attorney in favor of the banking signatory; a written operational substance report describing office facilities, staffing, and business activities; CV and local presence proof of the appointed manager or authorized officer; a board-approved AML/KYC policy manual; a commitment letter to supply annual audited accounts and tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent economic substance reporting for a Panama territorial-tax entity receiving worldwide digital income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed revenue-source breakdown demonstrating that taxable Panama-source activities are limited or properly ring-fenced; transfer pricing policy for the PIF's service arrangements; foreign tax credit calculation files where applicable; a Panama tax resident agent's memorandum on territorial taxation; operations calendar highlighting management and control in Panama if claimed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the PIF's Panama bank account must comply with general KYC and source-of-funds verification protocols. Recommended routing: founder's originating bank sends a SWIFT MT103 wire to the PIF's account at a licensed Panama bank using appropriate purpose codes such as 'Capital contribution to private interest foundation' or 'Initial foundation endowment'. The Panama bank will require the remitter to complete a funds-origin questionnaire, and the PIF must provide the Foundation Charter and council resolution authorizing the capital contribution. For amounts above approximately USD 10,000, enhanced due diligence reports are triggered; amounts above USD 100,000 may require additional written explanation of the wealth accumulation path. No exchange-control approval is required because Panama is fully dollarized, but the receiving bank may request clarification for unusually large or rapid injections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service disbursements from the PIF are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, commercial letters of credit (documentary credits), and, where appropriate, SWIFT MT202/MT205 for bank-to-bank transfers between the PIF's treasury accounts. The PIF must maintain a clear invoice ledger, signed disbursement instructions, and beneficial purchase records for each outgoing payment. For SaaS operational disbursements to vendors and contractors, ACH rails within Panama and SWIFT for international counterparties are acceptable. Periodic profit distributions or capital repatriations to the founder/beneficiaries must follow the foundation regulations and be supported by council resolutions and, where required, a tax report confirming territorial-source treatment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla EUR/USD forwards with a licensed Panama or offshore bank for non-Panama operating expenses
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settling Chinese vendor invoices where local currency controls prohibit physical delivery
Cross-currency interest rate swaps on the foundation's borrowed funds, subject to bank credit approval
Foreign exchange options and collars for protecting inbound founder capital contributions when the founder's tax residence currency appreciates against USD
FX swap agreements (swap-type outright transactions) for temporary liquidity conversions between USD, EUR, and GBP

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Flat Tax (Impuesto Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Ministry of Economy and Finance via Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each calendar year; for new foundations, first payment is due within 30 days after registration (pro-rated to the year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly interest of 0.5%; after 3 months, fines up to USD 500; prolonged default triggers administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) / DGI Transparency Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconfirmation by July 31; within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or foundation council composition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registered agent may be fined USD 500–USD 5,000; the foundation's registration may be suspended and the agent's license can be revoked

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de ISR) – Dormant or Zero Panamanian-Source Income Status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year end; based on RUC schedule for active businesses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines of USD 100–USD 500; non-filing can trigger presumed hidden income and lien registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Confirmation Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous/renewal confirmation must be evidenced in the foundation's public record before December 31 of each compliance year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a Panamanian registered agent for more than 30 days results in loss of good standing and an administrative strike-off proceeding

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Interest Foundations are exempt from statutory audit unless they derive Panamanian-source income exceeding USD 1,000,000 in a fiscal year (or hold consolidated assets above USD 1,500,000) or are expressly required by bank/financing agreements. Dormant foundations with no commercial activity never trigger an audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama GAAP (PCGA) applicable to non-financial entities; IFRS for SMEs permitted for internal records; IFRS full is mandatory for banks, brokerages, or regulated holding foundations. The foundation's records are private and not filed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain, update, and retain a Final Beneficial Owner declaration including the ultimate natural person(s). Any transfer of foundation economic rights or changes to the foundation council must be recorded in the agent's register within 30 days. Annually, by the DGI/Public Registry deadline, the agent must confirm via sworn statement that the register is current; unchanged structures may file a dormant confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Charter, Statutes and Amendments
Register of Foundation Council Members and Resolutions
Register of Beneficiaries and Final Beneficial Owners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0–1,500 (dormant); USD 2,500–5,000 if audit becomes mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on Panama-source net taxable income (Tax Code Article 699).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies (Tax Code Article 694): a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is subject to the 25% ISR only on Panama-source income. SaaS subscription fees from non-resident users collected via Stripe/Paddle and settled abroad are generally foreign-source and excluded from Panamanian ISR, giving a de facto 0% effective rate on purely offshore revenue. No general tax holidays apply to the no-code web builder scope. Limited preferential regimes (e.g., SEM multinational headquarters, reforestation, tourism) are not relevant to ISIC 6201. Distributions of accumulated foreign-source profits are tolled at the 10% beneficiary tax described below.
